content:
riley: FYI rolled a canary for "lazy-decoder-flush" in us-east-1 at 09:07 PT. idea: avoid full decoder state flush between rapid small requests to the same session to cut recompute for hot short flows. policy: keep decoder state sticky for sessions with >70% short-request ratio and <=6s inter-request gap.

meera: top-line numbers?

riley: quick 09:07-09:27 snapshot (5% traffic): requests 11.5k, p50 26ms -> 15ms (-42%), p95 290ms -> 175ms (-40%), p99 720ms -> 540ms (-25%). estimated cost per token -14%. error-rate stable.

devops-bot: deploy: runtime-service v5.8.2 -> canary(5%) (deploy id: d-20260322-09)

sam: great. any quality drift from sticky state? session bleed risk?

riley: ran session-consistency eval (3k traces). found a small class where very short followups inherited trailing tokens causing repeated words in the second response (~0.4% of samples). mitigation: we added a quick heuristic to hard-flush if next prompt contains explicit "STOP" tokens, multi-turn role swap (system->user), or length jump > +400 tokens. re-runs looked clean.

hana: KV cache interactions? last time sticky heuristics impacted warmup p99.

riley: KV path unchanged; sticky only affects decoder buffers in-GPU. microbench shows no additional KV misses; warmup improved slightly due to fewer cold recomputes.

product-bot: please add a console blurb and Route Analytics tile for "lazy-decoder sticky sessions" with projected savings and adoption.

sre-alert: alert rule added: lazy-decoder/us-east-1 p95 > baseline*1.6 -> notify @eng-oncall @eng-runtime; auto-rollback if error-rate > baseline*2 for 5m or p95 > baseline*1.8 for 3m.

meera: ramp plan?

riley: ramp 5% -> 30% in 12h if p95 stable -> 80% in 36h -> 100% in 72h. continuous lightweight A/B evals and dogfood window for product teams.

sam: action items: 1) extended evals on session-bleed edge cases (meera) 2) add console tile & blurb (riley/product) 3) monitor canary + synthetic session tests every 1m (sre) 4) coordinate a short note for enterprise customers (hana).

meera: thumbs up. will watch the synthetic tests and post any weird repetition cases here. :eyes:
